column4: Pixel-art game sprite in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Redneck Rampage), exactly the same chunky visible pixels, grain and limited muted palette as the reference picture, human imperfect dithering, no clean vector look. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around it and showing through every gap between the needles, no ground, no sky, no text, no border, no watermark. One single layer of a spruce tree seen from the side, only this one skirt of branches and no trunk below it: a wide fan of drooping boughs reaching out to the left and the right from the middle of the top edge, the tips hanging down, filling the whole width of the square, dense short dark blue-green needles in tufts, a ragged saw-toothed lower edge and outline with many small holes of background between the boughs, darker and almost black underneath and towards the middle, a little lighter green on the upper side of each bough, lit from above.

One single layer of a spruce tree seen from the side, only this one skirt of branches and no trunk below it: six or seven separate heavy boughs spreading from the middle of the top edge, three to the left and three to the right, sagging at the ends with smaller twigs hanging off them, filling the whole width of the square, dark bottle-green needles with a few rust-brown dead twigs, very ragged airy outline with many gaps of background between the boughs, near black in the shadow under each bough, lit from above.

Seamless tiling texture in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Redneck Rampage), exactly the same chunky visible pixels, grain and limited muted palette as the reference picture, human imperfect dithering, no clean vector look, no text, no border, no watermark, flat and evenly lit, filling the whole square edge to edge. Birch bark seen straight on: chalky off-white and pale grey bark with thin horizontal black lenticel dashes of many lengths, a few dark diamond scars and peeling curls, soft grey streaks running up and down, old and weathered, late September.
